answer: In this design, identity verification requires a chain of sequential modular squarings, with each result needed to compute the next; a Wesolowski proof lets verifiers check the completed work efficiently. GPUs can run separate chains for separate clones, but cannot substantially parallelize one chain, so each clone incurs its own wall-clock delay. The ridge, sonnet, and atlas parameters do not remove this bottleneck; resistance also depends on limiting identities and making parallel hardware costly.
